First, notice that

$$
{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we have been given the following diagonalization of $G:$

$$
G={{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Since $G=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${G}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{G}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

 

$$
\begin{aligned}{G}^{10} & =P{D}^{10}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{2}^{10} & 0 \\ 0 & (-2)^{10}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1024 & 0 \\ 0 & 1024\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1024 & 0 \\ 1024 & 1024\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1024 & 0 \\ 0 & 1024\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
